articleTitle: Digital Video Recording Techniques Using 1/2 Inch Metal Particle Tape
abstract: During the past ten years, rapid progress has been made in development of recording techniques for home use VTR. Nevertheless, a limit has now been reaches to improvement in such functional areas as SN ratio, resolution, and dubbing. It is now expected that digital recording techniques will be introduced into the video field in the future to assure even further development.

articleTitle: An Integrated 8 MHz Video Output Amplifier
abstract: An integrated 8 MHz video output amplifier is described, realized in a 280 V DMO6 process. Bandwidth, slew rate and internal protection against CRF flashover discharges are discussed. Operation without external heatsink and flexibility in application circuitry are emphasized.

articleTitle: A Home Automation System
abstract: A Home Automation (HA) System based on the Home Bus system has been developed. The system has a multi-layered hierachical structure and is composed of four subsystems (the Room Monitor Control Subsystem, the Telephone Subsystem, the Tele-control Subsystem and the In-house Video Control Subsystem). The HA system has both three inner-subsystem communication codes and one inter-subsystem communication code. The former are optimized for each subsystem and the latter enables the HA system to have efficiently combined applications. A compact (48.6 x 31 x 4 mm) communication control module which interfaces household appliances with the Home Bus has also been developed as one of the key parts for the system.

articleTitle: Development of CCD Imaging Block for Single Chip Color Camera
abstract: In recent years, the home use portable color camera and the camera recorder (VTR equipped with camera) market is getting larger. This kind of camera requires to be more compact and light-weighted, and to have a higher quality picture. CCD Image Sensor allows the camera to be small-sized and light-weighted, providing many advantages, such as low image lag, low image burning, precise image geometry, high resistance for magnetic field and mechanical vibration or shock, high stability and long life. However, they have problems peculiar to a solid-state imager, such as aliasing, cross color and necessity of precise three dimensional opto-mechanical locating between lens and CCD imager. To resolve these, CCD Imaging Block are developed. This realizes highly reliable and compact and light-weighted imaging system with high picture quality.

articleTitle: Improvement of Picture Quality for NTSC and PAL Systems by Digital Signal Processing
abstract: We have developed an intrafield picture quality improvement system within the existing TV standards.

articleTitle: A New Carrier Current Protocol Utilizing an Active Repeater for Consumer and Industrial Applications
abstract: A new protocol for carrier current networking systems utilizing an active repeater which has proven to be extremely reliable in energy management systems shows even greater promise for use in consumer applications.

articleTitle: Digital Signal Processing in Video Tape Recorders
abstract: Digital processing was successfully introduced into television sets by our system of VLSI circuits. It is the next logical step to replace the even more complicated analog processing in Video Tape Recorders (VTRs) of the well known systems (VHS, Beta, Video 2000) by digital means.

articleTitle: An Economical Digital Audio System for Consumer Delivery
abstract: A hybrid digital audio codec based on deltamodulation has been developed as an alternative to PCM. System gain and emphasis are dynamically variable under control of a sophisticated companding algorithm; separate control bit-streams are generated for subsequent transmission to the decoder. The system offers high quality audio performance at overall bit rates of 250-350 kb/s/channel.

articleTitle: A Color Video Printer with Sublimation Dye Transfer Method
abstract: In accordance with the recent progress in the video application sector such as video discs, still video floppy, electronic still video camera and hi-resoluti on VCR, the need for getting hard copies from these video signals is expanding.

articleTitle: Electrostatic Discharge Protection in Linear Ics
abstract: Damage due to electrostatic discharge (ESD) is one of the main causes of failure in the use of bipolar ICs. The principal failure mechanism is found to be short-circuiting of the B-E junction. A number of protection structures, realized with an 18V linear process, were characterized by testing them with a structure having a damage voltage, Vdam, lower than 400V. The Vdam of the protected structure is a good index of the quality of the protection structure and permits a comparison of the various solutions. Protection structures with Vdam in the range 3000V to 9000V are presented.

articleTitle: System and Realization aspects of Multistandard TV Receivers
abstract: With the advent of cable and satellite TV demand for multistandard TV-receivers has grown rapidly. The introduction of multichannel sound systems leads to a greater complexity of TV-receivers. At the same time the demands on picture and sound processing have been increased.

articleTitle: Fast Switching Frequency Synthesizer Employing Adaptive Phase Locked Loop
abstract: This work describes a fast switching frequency synthesizer employing an adaptive second order phase locked loop whose damping ratio is taken as ζ=0.707 while its natural frequency could be varied according to the step change in the division ratio of the programable counter to improve the switching time for large step change in the division ratio without degrading the noise rejection properties. The mathematical relationship which describes the behaviour of the system is carried out and the system is implemented assuming certain design values. The response of the system is obtained to show that the step change in the division ratio could be increased to ten times without skipping cycles in the loop.

articleTitle: Integrated Video Output Stages for Direct Driving of Color Tube Cathodes
abstract: At the beginning of 1980 the combination of high voltage technology and special field plate techniques allowed the integration of the first RGB video output amplifier ICs capable of withstanding supply voltages up to 200V. Further work has resulted in the development of a new integrated RGB video amplifier, the technological and electrical solutions of which are presented here.

articleTitle: Picture Signal Improvement in Coloyr TV Receivers
Using Extensions to World System Teletext
abstract: World System Teletext is now well established as a reliable and economical information service in the consumer environment. Over seven million teletext decoders are now in use in various parts of the world, using the basic teletext transmissions which have been in service since 1976.

articleTitle: A Color Flat Cathode Ray Tube
abstract: Recently, rapid advances have been made in flat-panel displays, such as Liquid Crystal Displays, Plasma Displays, Electroluminescent Displays, Vacuum Fluorescent Displays and so on. Applications to flat TV displays have been seriously considered. No flat displays, however, can meet all the necessary requirement for TV displays, especially the color TV displays. Compared to conventional CRT displays, numerous problems still remain in regard to brightness, contrast, cosmetics, resolution, driving power, power consumption, cost performance and reliability.

articleTitle: Defined-Format Teletext Moves to Higher Levels of Display and Yet Fulfils ITS Promise of Compatibility with First Generation Decoders
abstract: This paper discusses how the World System Teletext specification is fully compatible with the higher levels of display defined in the new CEPT Videotex 'presentation layer' standard. Careful design of transmission coding results in a system that is both efficient and rugged and yet permits full downwards compatibility with the many first-generation World System Teletext decoders that are installed throughout the world.

articleTitle: The Development of Multi-Media Terminals in NTT
New Video Doc System with Miniaturized Low Frequency Saw Device in Home VTR
abstract: A new dropout compensation system with miniaturized low frequency SAW device has been developed, corresponding with the stream of high density magnetic recording.

articleTitle: The 5-Inch Size Full Color Liquid Crystal Television Addressed by Amorphous Silicon Thin Film Transistors
abstract: In recent years, development of LCD'S has progressed remarkably and have been widely applied in various equipment. For example, a mono-chromatic LCD TV receiver has already appeared in the Japanese market.

articleTitle: Digital Still Picture Recorder Utilizing an Ordinary Audio Cassette Deck
abstract: This paper describes a new digital still picture recording system utilizing an ordinary audio cassette tape.

articleTitle: Advances in 3-Volt Lithium Batteries for Electronic Applications
abstract: Significant improvements have been made in recent years in the performance, reliability and operating temperature range of 3-volt primary lithium cell systems. Because of their excellent characteristics, especially their long life, they are not only being used in devices in which they are consumer replaceable, but also in devices in which they are hard wired and expected to last the useful life of the device. Thus, a new option is now available to the device designer who needs to incorporate a small power source in his design. Typical coin cells which can be supplied with customized terminals for hand or wave soldering are shown in Figure 1.

articleTitle: A New Tape Path Analysis System for All VCR Tape Transport Systems
abstract: The sale of 8mm VCR with mounted camera started in the U. S. A. in 1984. One of the most-important items that remained to be developed was a tape transport system suitable for smaller, lighter, and easier-to- handle portable VCRs, and to achieve an automatic-tape path alignment system as well as a non-alignment system.

articleTitle: Application Proposals for Multistandard Sound TV-Receivers
abstract: The growing number of multichannel tv sound standards may give one the impression that the national standardization authorities are tying a new Gordian knot. Certainly it has created many new problems for tv set manufacturers who are developing multistandard receivers.

articleTitle: Symmetric Line Deflection for Colour TV Receivers with Enhanced Picture Quality
abstract: Colour T. V. receivers featuring a significantly improved picture quality in many cases work with an increased line scanning frequency. The principle of bidirectional line scan with a sinusoidal deflection current can be applied with advantage. The problems of this horizontal scanning method are discussed and solutions are proposed, the feasibility of which is shown with a laboratory model.

articleTitle: TV Multichannel Sound - The BTSC System
abstract: In late 1978, the Broadcast Television System Committee of the Electronic Industries Association, on behalf of the television industry, formed a subcommittee for the purpose of formulating standards for the broadcasting and reception of multichannel television sound which was to include stereophonic as well as second program (second language, for example) enhancements of the main audio program. On December 22, 1983, the industry chose the Zenith transmission system coupled with the dbx noise reduction system and submitted the combined system, the BTSC system, to the Federal Communications Commission on January 30, 1984. On April 23, 1984, the FCC released a Report and Order in Docket No. 21323 wherein the choice of technical standards was left to the marketplace, but protection was afforded to the pilot frequency of the BTSC system. In addition, if a pilot is transmitted at 15.734 kHz, the BTSC system must be employed as described in the FCC office of Science and Technology Bulletin No. 60.

articleTitle: High Resolution Electronic Still Camera with Two Mos Imagers
abstract: The electronic still camera is a new concept in cameras, which uses solid state imagers to convert the light from the object into picture information in the form of electrical signals which then stored on a video floppy inside the camera.

articleTitle: A 10-Bit 65MSPS Glitch-free Video D/A Converter
abstract: In these days digital signal processing of video signal has become popular due to the development of monolithic video D/A and A/D converter. It is said that 8 bits resolution is sufficient for real time video signal processing such as digital T.V. application, however, 9 to 10 bits resolution is required to the use of digital VTR, camera and studio equipments.

articleTitle: Video Recording with New Signal Processing
abstract: Video recording systems such as VTRs generally use an emphasis method in signal processing to reduce noise generated in FM recording and reproduction, using a pre-emphasis circuit and a de-emphasis circuit. In recording, the high frequency components of the video signal are emphasized by the pre-emphasis circuit and, in reproduction, the emphasized components are suppressed by exactly the same amount by the de-emphasis circuit; this is very effective in reducing the FM noise, especially its high frequency components.

articleTitle: A Novel High-Dynamic-Range PLL System for Synchronous Detection in AM Receivers
abstract: This paper presents a novel nested phase-lock loop system for synchronous detection in AM radio receivers with frequency-synthesizer tuning. The VCXO of the phase-lock loop simultaneously acts as the reference frequency for the synthesizer. A unique compensation technique that ties the poles of the PLL transfer function down in fixed positions effectuates an extremely high dynamic range, thereby alleviating the i. f. filter requirements drastically. With a loop bandwidth of 3.5Hz, an interfering carrier with a 50dB higher level and at a distance of 9kHz from the desired carrier is adequately rejected.

articleTitle: An Integrated High Performance Synchronization Processor

authors.preferredName: A. C. J. G. Van De Waterlaat

abstract: Until now the architecture of T. V. sets has been established with respect to off air reception. Now however, signals from peripheral equipment such as video recorders, camera's, games and TXT decoders must also be handled.

articleTitle: Voc(*): An Integrated High Quality Speech Synthesizer Based on LPC Techniques
abstract: The electronic synthesis of human speech represents another step in the evolution of the man-machine interface.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wide Viewing Angle Rear Projection Television Screen
abstract: Consumer based rear projection television (PTV) systems are composed of three CRTs which form the red, green and blue portions of the TV picture. Three projection lenses magnify these images and converge them into a single plane. The viewing screen is placed in this plane.

articleTitle: Pulse Shape Optimization and Channel Equalization for Teletext Transmission Over Multipath Channels
abstract: A study of teletext transmission over multipath channels is reported. Computer simulacted results are used to ineasure the perfornmance of various Nvquist pulses. An optimal ptulse shape for teletext transmission is obtained.

articleTitle: Intelligent Mask-programmable Crt-processor
abstract: This paper describes a mask-programmable CRT-processor (CRTP) which is a display control system provided with graphics/text display functions and various intelligent graphic drawing functions. This CRTP is a powerful tool for rapid development of customized VLSIs for high-performance display control systems.

articleTitle: Automated Testing of Cable Television Converters
Effect of Microlens Array for Mos Color Imager
abstract: A high-photosensitivity and well-balanced color reproduction color imager with a monolithic microlens array was developed. The microlens array was formed on a 2/3-inch MOS color imager using a photolithographic technique with a transparent photoresist. The microlens array was arranged on the top of only the green portions of the mosaic filter (G-lens array) of the color imager. For an imager with a 2.0-um thick G-lens, the photosensitivity was raised 25% over the relative response of the green signal for an imager without a G-lens array, and the color image reproduced by the G-lens imager was better balanced than that of the original device.

articleTitle: 1.3 GHz Pll With 12C.Bus
abstract: A single chip PLL IC for digital tuning application up to 1.3 GHz is described. It is part of a new family of analog and digital TV-ICs, which are functionally controlled via a common 2-wire bi-directional I2C Bus (Inter-Integrated Circuit Bus) by a single chip microcomputer.

articleTitle: TV Multichannel Audio - A Chipset for US Stereo TV Receivers Using Digital Signal Processing
abstract: In 1984 the US Federal Communications Commission officially approved stereo broadcasting for television. The EIA's Broadcast Television Systems Commitee recommended a multichannel-TV-sound-system including companding techniques. This BTSC-System has emerged as the standard for US.

articleTitle: An Integrated Serial Bus Architecture: Principles and Applications
An Analysis of and Human Factor Study on Access Delay Time to Home Bus
abstract: Various information systems such as one-line key-telephone systems and security alarm systems are found in a home. For efficient installation, a home bus, which manages signals and information, is required. To realize the home bus, specifications must be determined in consideration of many design conditions.

articleTitle: High Frequency Saw Filters Stretched Over Non-Overlapped Electrodes for Satellite Broadcast Receivers
abstract: We have developed a new UHF SAW filter for satellite broadcast receivers. The features are a high center frequency which suppresses image interference, sufficiently flat group delay for linear FM detection, and no necessity to adjust for tuning.

articleTitle: A Lower Power Up-conversion Frequency Synthesizer for AM/FM/WB/SW Applications
abstract: The conventional superhetrodyne AM receiver utilizing a 260 to 450 KHz Intermediate Frequency has been with us since its invention in the 1920's. The block diagram shown in fig. 1 has typified automobile radio design: an RF amplifier drives two tuned circuits which are necessary to protect the mixer from cross-modulation from nearby strong signals, and a local oscillator to produce the desired IF. Although widely implemented, this approach is expensive because of the severe requirements placed on the varactor tuning diodes, and the excessive number of adjustments.

articleTitle: Modem IC Supports Three 1200 BPS Standards
abstract: The popularity of personal computers have created a greater need for more efficient and inexpensive communication methods between computers. The existence of different protocols made the problem more complex. This paper recommends a solution by using an IC modem device that supports the three major 1200 bps protocols. This paper also discusses the design flexibility achieved by using such a modem device.

articleTitle: Digital (PCM) Tuner for Reception of BIGFON Signals
abstract: The "Deutsche Bundespost" (German Federal Mail Service), in co-operation with several electronics companies, have installed experimental BIGFON systems in various towns of the Federal Republic of Germany (BIGFON is the German abbreviation for "broadband integrated optical fibre local communication network").

articleTitle: Two IC's for Teletext Data Demodulation
abstract: A new IC kit for demodulation of teletext data has been designed in order to have a good adaptability for various standards. This IC's require a low number of external components.

articleTitle: A Compatible and Economical 3-D TV System
abstract: A different technique for realising a 3-D perspective of pictures on the existing TV receivers is presented in this paper. Two images of a 3-D object are produced and transmitted, one of the two during the odd field and the other during the even field of an interlaced-scanned TV system. An inexpensive electronic logic module, added at the transmitting and receiving ends, controls the multiplexing and demultiplexing of the video signals without any modifications to the TV signal standards. This technique uses a Field Masking Synchronous Shutter (FMSS) for realisation of 3-D perspective. This also overcomes the limitations posed by the use of color filters in the earlier proposals. The cost performance factor of the new scheme makes its implementation attractive for both Color and Black and White (B/W) TV systems.

articleTitle: Naplps Videotex Frame Creation System with Automatic Encoding fo Input Images
abstract: NAPLPS (North American Presentation Level Protocol Syntax), recommended by CCITT as a world VIDEOTEX standard, is already being utilized commercially. The NAPLPS system is distinguished by: 1. Its high degree of hardware independence. New decoders with new functions made possible by advances in hardware technology will still be able to decode old NAPLPS data. This is important for the building of data bases. 2. A geometrical code with a high level of abstraction, making it possible to compress transmitted data. Images are drawn using geometrical elements such as points, lines, rectangles, arcs, and polygons, so a large amount of detail can be represented by a small amount of data.

articleTitle: Cable Isolation
A Cost-Effective Digital Decoder for PAL Signals
abstract: Three conditions are proposed to examine the efficiency of decoding PAL signals based on a certain sampling structure. Analysis shows that the fs =4fsc is the best structure for digital PAL decoding, and there still exists potential of improvement on 4fsc decoder, A new comb filter is then developed, which can reduce both delay units and their throughput rates by half, and therefore make the decoder cost-effective.

articleTitle: Interconnection of Cable Television and Consumer Electronics Devices
abstract: The cable television industry and the consumer electronics industry have, until very recently, developed their products with little regard to each other. FCC regulations on technical cable system performance levels have provided the only definition of the interface between the cable operator and the consumer's terminal equipment.

articleTitle: EMC Regulations and Methods of Measurement for Sound and Television Broadcast Receivers in the Federal Republic of Germany
abstract: Up to 1981 only the capability of active interfering, e.g. the interfering radiation power of the receivers, by which other radio services may be affected, was limited by the regulations substantially. But the time before the number of registered cases, where receivers were affected by other sevices, mainly by the CB-service, increased year after year (from about 5 600 in 1976 up to more than 11 000 in 1979). Based on this fact in 1981 the technical regulations for broadcast receivers have been supplemented by EMC regulations so that the receivers additionally must follow minimum values of immunity against interference under normal conditions.

articleTitle: Power Transformers for Switched Mode Power Supplies
abstract: The magnetic circuit of power transformers for switched mode power supplies is analyzed, and formulas are derived. A counter-biasing permanent magnet may be included in the magnetic circuit to increase the range of utilization of the magnetic saturated flux density Bs of the ferrite cores. The working principle of such counter-biasing magnets are discussed.

articleTitle: Data Detection from Deteriorated Eye Patterns
abstract: This paper describes how to achieve accurate data detection from deteriorated eye patterns suffering from both linear and non-linear distortion. Either of two threshold levels is selected for reading deteriorated data in the amplitude direction (data regeneration), and three different timing are used for reading deteriorated data in the time-domain direction (data retiming). The new data detection system combines these regenerating and retiming techniques. This system has enabled us to develop a digital recording system for use with a VCR in the slow EP mode.

articleTitle: A Digital Color Video Camera Using A Single-Chip Solid-STate Image Sensor
abstract: Recent progress in the field of digital ICs and LSIs has brought digital television/video circuitry almost a reality consumer applica-tions, but not quite. Although there have been several papers describing digital signal processing for consumer video cameras,1)2) there remains a number of problems to be soloved before making these cameras viable. Higher speed, higher accuracy and lower power consumption, for instance, are required for an ADC. The yield rate of image sensors are to be improved substantially.

articleTitle: A New Intelligent Remote Control Unit for Consumer Electronic Devices
abstract: Means like menu-techniques or so called help-files for simplifying the handling of various appliances have gained a firm footing in most fields of professional or semi-professional technology. Evidently this trend will extend even to the smallest microprocessor equipped professional device. Only in the field of consumer electronics, where even a timer controlled video cassette recorder has proven to be a technically very complicated machine, no realy drastic progress is visible. Instead extremely difficult to handle appliances which require large instruction manuals are still developed and marketed. Here a large number of switches and buttons dominate, though an intelligent application of the principles of "user-guidance" already known today would allow simple and self-explanatory control units.

articleTitle: TV Power Processor I.C. Master Slave Concept
abstract: A new concept of TV power processor is described. Switched Mode Power Supply drive and self starting are realized in a primary located circuit, while horizontal frame and SMPS functions such regulation and synchronization are performed on a secondary located circuit. All power transfers, in particular the frame, are in switched mode allowing improved performances and cost reduction.

articleTitle: A Fully Automatic Multistandard TV Chrominance Decoder
abstract: An automatic multistandard TV chrominance decoder IC (NTSC 3,58 MHz and 4,43 MHz, Pal and Secam) has been developed.

articleTitle: Swithced-Capacitor Stereo Decoders for T.V. and Radio Receivers
abstract: Conventional stereo decoder i.c.'s require many off-chip components and several adjustments. This paper describes two stereo-decoder i.c.'s, which use switched-capacitor techniques to allow full integration and elimination of adjustments. The first decoder is a decoder for television receivers which are based on the so-called "two-carrier" system (1). A second sound carrier is used here, that contains stereo information in the case of "stereo-mode", or information which is independent of that in the first channel, for instance a second languaoe, in the case of "dual mode". The second decoder is an fm-stereo-multiplex decoder for f.m.-radio receivers, which decodes a multiplex signal into a "left" and a "right" signal. A new system approach not only resulted here in full integration, but also in an improved specification. This approach can also be used for stereo decoders for t.v. receivers which are based upon a multiplex system, like for instance the recommended system in America (2).

articleTitle: Enhancing the Sound and Colour Capabilities of Home Computers
abstract: This paper discusses system implications of a new integrated 64 colour video encoder for NTSC and PAL standards, and the capabilities of a new LSI stereo sound processor. The consequential challenge to generate enhanced applications software is also considered.

articleTitle: Vertical Deflection Booster with Automatic Raster Size Compensation
abstract: As the circuit complexity of modern TV receivers increases, the advantages of concentrating as many low signal functions as possible into one IC become more and more evident. These are functions which can all be realized using the same technology and they should be separated from the interface circuits which are capable of handling high power.

articleTitle: Hands Free Telephone Conversations are Simplified Using New Integrated Circuits
abstract: Speakerphones wer e desi gned by Bell Labs, in the 1950's for use with their telephones in order to provide hands free operation of a telephone. The original usage ended up primarily as business applications since it was found that the concept of hands free telephones appealed to executives, and anyone who considered himself to be an executive.

articleTitle: An Ultra Low Power 500MHz Dual Modulus Prescaler
abstract: Frequency synthesized tunning system utlizing Phase Locked Loop (PLL) technique has been used in many kinds of communication fields due to the stability and accuracy. Recently this system has been adopted in consumer and communication fields used a battery type supply, for example, cordless telephone and personal radio and so on. Therefore, the drastic improvement concerning about power saving and physical dimensions of the system has been strongly required. However, in the conventional technique, the approach for the reduction of power consumption has been realized at a typical 5V operation.

articleTitle: Subscription Teletext for Value Added Services
abstract: Teletext is rapidly becoming a household name in many countries in Europe. Its success is partly because it can provide instant information to anyone with a suitable decoder free of charge. In the UK, teletext services are financed either from the licence fee (Ceefax) or from advertising revenue (Oracle). Videotex systems such as Prestel make use of the public telephone network and are interactive and can be financed by charging the user directly. The user pays for the telephone connection, computer time and the information. These costs can be prohibitive particularly when terminals remain connected throughout the day.

articleTitle: Picture Transmission for Videotex
abstract: Videotex system is an interactive two-way information retrieval system providing a host of information from its vast database via the telephone network. It allows the subscriber to request information by dialling up the videotex computer; select pages of text and pictorial information and have them displayed on the screens of adapted home television sets.

articleTitle: Sound PCM Decoder LSls for Japanese DBS
abstract: This paper describes sound PCM decoder LSIs used for 12GHz TV direct broadcasting via satellite (DBS). These LSIs include newly developed data processing circuits, such as sync detector, RAM controller, de-interleaver, error corrector etc. Functions and features of these circuits are explained in detail.

articleTitle: EMI Caused by Line Deflection Circuits
abstract: Rapid rate of change of current in the fall time of transistors and the forward and reverse recovery time of diodes often gives rise to radiated electromagnetic interference repeated at horizontal frequency. When surface acoustic wave filters are used, scan bars are sometimes produced on the screen as a result of triple transit echoes of the received noises. Compromises should often be made between receiving sensitivity power loss, and electromagnetic compatibility.

articleTitle: Multi-Track PCM Audio Utilizing 8 mm Video System
abstract: The 8mm Video system can realize the smaller-size & lighter-weight design, the better sound quality and the better picture quality than conventional VCRs.

articleTitle: Mask Programmable Filters: A New Concept for Monolithic Switched Capacitor Filters
A Novel System for Music Synthesis Using A Digital Sound Processor IC
abstract: A 16-channel, polyphonic and polytimbric, fully digital sound processor IC for music synthesis is described. It is microprocessor-controlled and the coded music information is resident in an external memory.

articleTitle: A Self-Adapting Driver Circuit for Horizontal TV Deflection
abstract: A new approach for the driver circuit* of the horizontal deflection in TV and monitor chassis was realized in a small power IC. The concept avoids the classical driver transformer and is widely independent of the different applications and deflection frequencies. The element provides an optimum charge and discharge current for the discrete power transistor and reduces the total power consumption of the deflection. Various control functions are implemented and take care of the safe operating conditions of the power element in the turn ON and OFF transient phase of the chassis. This improves the reliability of the system significantly.

articleTitle: Skipper: A Prototype Expert System
abstract: In recent years, the business and industrial community has begun to take considerable interest in concepts, techniques, and systems developed by researchers in artificial intelligence. In particular, ezpert systems have been explored for application to a wide range of real-world problems. An expert system is a computer program which emulates the lines of reasoning used by a human expert to solve problems in a narrowly defined domain of expertise. For example, MYCIN[1], an expert system developed at Stanford, makes recommendations to a physician regarding the diagnosis of meningitis and related diseases. Commonly (though not universally) an expert system is able to explain its "reasoning" in terms understandable by those expected to use the system. These users may or may not be knowledgeable in the field, but they are not expected to be computer programmers.

articleTitle: Horizontal & Vertical Deflection Combinations for Monitors
abstract: Many of the integrated circuits for deflection utilized in monitors and video displays are TV application oriented. However, the monitor market is becoming more and more important, sufficiently so to justify the development of integrated circuits specifically aimed at satisfying the specific requirements of this field.

articleTitle: Suggested Design Techniques for Telephone Equipment Requiring Canadian Certification
abstract: The Terminal Attachment Program Advisory Committee (TAPAC) is responsible for setting up technical requirements for customer provided devices which are intended for connection to the TWX, Telex or Public Telephone Networks under Federal jurisdiction in Canada, to ensure that network harm does not result.

articleTitle: Flicker-Free Non Interlaced Receiving System for Standard Color TV Signals
abstract: The television signals are sampled both spatially and temporally, i. e., the vertical domain of the image is quantized by scanning lines, while the temporal domain according to the time rate of the field alterations. In that consequence, parasitic specta are introduced in the sampled product, and in principle, a pre-filter and an interpolation filter based on sampling theory are necessarily called for to the faithful reproduction of original picture quality at the displays.

articleTitle: Scanning Modes for Flicker-Free Colour TV-Reproduction
abstract: In this paper some scanning and processing methods for flicker free high quality TV reproduction are compared with respect to picture quality. Among these methods-which have been already published-are progressive scan reproduction by either field insertion or temporal field interpolation and a frame repetition technique. It comes out, that progressive scan reproduction by field insertion techniques is superior with respect to still and moving picture areas and with respect of chrominance/luminance separation.

articleTitle: Quality Improvement by Adaptive Inter-/Intraframe Processing in Pal TV Receivers
abstract: Conceptions for digital colour TV receivers open the way to substantially improved TV pictures. Utilizing field or frame store units, it will be possible to realize three-dimensional filters, which exploit special properties of PAL-or NTSC-signals for an efficient reduction of present disturbances [1]. These impairments, mainly caused by-cross effects between luminance and chrominance information-noise of various sources, and-flicker effects, can be completely eliminated for lots of picture contents. However, with special scene detail, this elimination is not sufficient, moreover, three-dimensional filtering will evoke additional disturbing effects, for an example blurring of edges. Therefore, an adaptively controlled use of these complex filters is necessary to avoid additional degradation and to achieve overall good performance.

articleTitle: A New 5.3V" High-Brightness Beam-Index Display
abstract: A beam-index color CRT has a number of advantages over a conventional color tube.1~7 For example the conventional color tube is less bright than a beam-index color tube. And in a conventional tube, when the cathode current and the accelerated-voltage are raised in order to get more brightness, nearly 80% of the energy is absorbed by the mask, so the mask becomes warped and the beam doesn't land correctly.

articleTitle: A High Performance, High Efficiency Audio Subsystem for Car Ratio
abstract: An electronic module designed for locally powered loudspeakers in OEM autosound applications has evolved from a circuit that employed small scale off-the-shelf ICs and many discrete components, ttough a revision utilizing semi-custom ICs and fewer discretes, to an advanced realization that capitalizes on the benefits of full custom integration. This paper first considers the unique requirements placed on high fidelity music systems by automotive application, and describes a particular system solution that specifies a compact electronic circuit. Implementation of the circuit functions with the full custom ICs is then discussed, followed by a presentation of the measured performance of the circuit.

articleTitle: New Services and Technologies for Digital Telephone Sets
abstract: As the first step toward developing, the "Information Network System (INS)",(1) a pilot plant called the "INS Model System",(2) which provides a fully digitized end-to-end connection between customer equipment, is now being tested in the Musashino/Mitaka area in Tokyo.

articleTitle: A New Integrated High-Performance AM Receiver for Car Radio
abstract: A new type of monolithic AM receiver has been designed and integrated in a conventional 40OMHz-fT bipolar process. Adjustments and band switches are completely eliminated, and production costs can be reduced considerably thanks to the unconventional approach, which uses an upconversion system.

articleTitle: A HIGH-Speed Packet-Switching Network for CATV Systems
abstract: A high-speed packet-switched metropolitan area network can be built on a residential cable television (CATV) system. The-goal of such a system is to extend the local area network environment from the office to the home. This paper presents an overview of communications to the home via CATV and proposes specific methods of utilizing the residential CATV system to bring high performance communication to the home.

articleTitle: 1985 Index IEEE Transactions on Consumer Electronics Vol. CE-31
abstract: This index covers all technical items - papers, correspondence, reviews, etc. - that appeared in this periodical during the year, and items from previous years that were commented upon or corrected in this year. Departments and other items may also be covered if they have been judged to have archival value. The Author Index contains the primary entry for each item, listed under the first author's name. The primary entry includes the coauthors' names, the title of the paper or other item, and its location, specified by the publication abbreviation, year, month, and inclusive pagination. The Subject Index contains entries describing the item under all appropriate subject headings, plus the first author's name, the publication abbreviation, month, and year, and inclusive pages. Note that the item title is found only under the primary entry in the Author Index.
